mechanisms.reason: Publication, confirmation, effect and acknowledgement are ordered explicitly. Unique operation records close crash/race gaps; per-entity serialization and admission controls explain how failures change work.

coherence.reason: Receipt generation connects all cards, progressing from observable asynchronous outcomes to actors, duplicate protection, retries, ordering, overload and queue/log choice. Transactions, uniqueness and rate arithmetic are declared prerequisites.

decisions.reason: The learner can choose synchronous authorization, deferred generation, transient versus permanent recovery, serialization scope and queue versus retained history while stating operating, latency and capacity costs.

clarity.reason: Roles and new concepts are defined through concrete actions; the offsets and partition example supplies the otherwise unfamiliar log prerequisites. Arithmetic and crash examples support transfer without excessive detail.

outcomes.reason: Maps API/broker/worker, waits for confirmed handoff, separates saved ready result from broker acknowledgement, exposes pending/ready/failed status, retains synchronous access dependency and names broker/worker and status costs.

Explains post-commit redelivery and pre-effect acknowledgement loss; stable IDs, uniqueness and a durable transaction combine credit with duplicate detection. Repeats skip the credit without claiming exactly-once delivery or external effects.

Retries plausible outages with growing delay and finite budget, immediately isolates persistent invalid input, exposes exhausted failures, preserves healthy progress and checks cause and prior effects before replay.

Calculates the wrong final value of 5 from reordered effects, distinguishes delivery from completion, serializes an item across retries, permits other items in parallel and identifies the hot-item throughput limit.

Computes 40 additional jobs per second, links oldest-job age to missed completion promises, bounds workers at the saturated store, visibly throttles/rejects admission, limits buffering by time/storage/retention and conditions worker scaling on downstream headroom.

Explains competing workers divide jobs, independent groups each consume events, within-group partition sharing and per-group positions. Offset commit does not delete events; replay requires retained records. Neither partitions nor progress imply global order or exactly-once external effects.

sourceChecks.claim: Asynchronous Request-Reply separates initial acceptance from long-running work and describes status polling and delayed failure. The lesson correctly restricts deferral to callers that can proceed without the result.
RabbitMQ explicitly states publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements are independent and cover different interactions. The flow diagram and durability qualification match that distinction.

AWS idempotent-API guidance requires stable caller/request identity and atomic token-plus-mutation processing. The unique processed-jobs transaction protects database effects but does not extend to unrelated external effects.

Azure Retry distinguishes transient from persistent failures, bounded attempts and delayed retries. The linked lesson sources Competing Consumers and Queue-Based Load Leveling additionally support isolating poison jobs for investigation and deliberate resubmission.

Competing Consumers warns about ordering with concurrent consumers and describes ordered message sessions. The old/new overwrite and serialization-through-retries rule are valid concrete consequences, not an automatic queue guarantee.

Queue-Based Load Leveling explicitly warns that excessive average arrival rate grows backlog, downstream concurrency needs bounds, storage/retention are finite and producer shedding may be required. The arithmetic and scaling conditions match.

Kafka Design documents per-group partition ownership and offsets, deliberate rewind, retained-log deletion policies and scoped transaction semantics. The diagram shows independent applications and the prose correctly limits replay and ordering.
